value.livesOn: The town runs on offshore sub-sea survey contracts and deep-water acoustic telemetry. Coreline Instruments owns the deep-water testing buoys and sensor arrays anchored across the shelf, while the local salvage crews and drydock mechanics keep their uncrewed survey vessels, tether lines, and seabed probes running day and night.
value.happened: Three weeks ago an automated deep-trench probe popped back to the surface off the breakers six months early, completely scorched, with its onboard optical telemetry core still transmitting encrypted pings. Coreline's salvage crew locked down the main quay to haul it in, but half the data canisters broke loose in the surf before they could secure the rig.
value.stake: The physical telemetry core from the scorched probe, which is currently wedged in a submerged cable tangle under the old crane pier.

sides.name: Coreline Operations
sides.wants: To lock down the entire shoreline, recover every lost telemetry capsule, and keep the probe data sealed away from external auditors.

sides.name: The Basin Salvage Pool
sides.wants: To dredge up the telemetry core themselves, crack the survey data, and sell the seabed anomaly coordinates on the open market to clear their dock debts.

common: The deep sonar array off the north shelf never shuts down, and that hum comes right through the floorboards at low tide.
Watch your step along the south conduit: the salt mist shorts the outdoor junction boxes every time the wind turns.
The divers in the red coveralls work for Coreline, and they don't drink on the same side of the pier as the crane operators.
If you find a sealed telemetry canister washed up in the kelp, don't crack the casing or you'll have four corporate goons on your neck by morning.
The old boatyard was supposed to be a municipal marina until the telemetry firm bought the lease right out from under the council.

value.title: The Scorched Telemetry
value.summary: We picked up the telemetry broadcast from the scorched deep-trench probe before Coreline could jam the frequency, but the decryption key is fragmented across the dock logs. I need someone to pull the coordinates from my terminal, check with the crew at Instance 9, and retrieve the telemetry canister from Instance 13 before the corporate divers sweep the quay.

steps.objective: Get the screen code out of Person 10 at Instance 52.
Access the locked desk screen at Instance 52 in Zone 1
Talk to Person 8 at Instance 9 in Zone 1
Take Thing 7 from Instance 13 in Zone 1
Give Thing 7 to Person 10 at Instance 52 in Zone 1

value.title: Survey Manifest Run
value.summary: I left my survey gear manifest over at the warehouse during the morning unload, and I cannot leave the bar until the tender clears the lock. Go over to Instance 13, clear it with Person 9, and bring Thing 7 back to me.

steps.objective: Give Thing 7 to Person 8 at Instance 9

value.title: Dampening the Shelf Hum
value.summary: The sub-shelf telemetry hum is vibrating right through our floorboards at low tide. Person 8 over at Instance 9 mentioned an unclaimed acoustic buffer sitting over in Instance 13, but nobody here has the legs to go retrieve it past the dock patrol.

steps.objective: Deliver Thing 7 to Person 10 at Instance 52

value.title: The South Conduit Log
value.summary: The conduit logs from the south pier were locked up in the warehouse before our shift turned over. Person 9 won't hand over the crate without a bottle from the taproom, so get a bottle of Thing 6 from Person 1 at Instance 9, trade it for Thing 7 at Instance 13, and bring it back here.

steps.objective: Talk to Person 10 at Instance 52 in Zone 1.
Buy Thing 6 from Person 1 at Instance 9 in Zone 1.
Give Person 9 Thing 6 at Instance 13 in Zone 1.
Take Thing 7 from Instance 13 in Zone 1.
Give Person 10 Thing 7 at Instance 52 in Zone 1.

value.title: Basin Transducer Run
value.summary: The acoustic pinging from the shelf buoys is rattling the glass right out of my sashes. Person 8 borrowed my spare transducer clamp down at Instance 9, but word is he left it in storage over at Instance 13. Go track down Thing 7 and bring it back so I can bolt the frame down before high tide.

steps.objective: Walk 120 metres to Instance 9 in Zone 1.
Walk 90 metres back to Instance 52 in Zone 1.

value.title: Sub-Sea Acoustic Registry
value.summary: I can't step out onto the lane while Coreline patrol crews are monitoring the junction boxes outside. I need you to unlock my desk terminal, pull the logged telemetry packet, and carry Thing 8 across to Person 9 at Instance 13 before the Basin salvage pool sweeps the dock.

steps.objective: Get the screen code out of Person 10 at Instance 52.
Decrypt the desk screen at Instance 52
Walk 90 metres to Instance 13 in Zone 1
Deliver Thing 8 to Person 9 at Instance 13
Report back to Person 10 at Instance 52

value.title: Acoustic Filter Courier
value.summary: I can't leave the warehouse watch while the Coreline canisters are still being sorted, but Person 1 over at the bar is holding onto the diagnostic cable I need. Head across to Instance 9, grab Thing 2, and bring it back to me.

steps.objective: Talk to Person 9 at Instance 13 about the telemetry filter.
Talk to Person 1 at Instance 9 about Thing 2.
Deliver Thing 2 to Person 9 at Instance 13.

value.title: Acoustic Gear Drop
value.summary: I can't step away from Instance 9 while the telemetry crew is keeping tabs on everyone off shift. I need someone to head 70 metres over to Instance 13, pick up Thing 7, and get it across to Person 10 at Instance 52 before the dock managers notice it cleared the floor.

steps.objective: Speak with Person 8 in Instance 9, Zone 1
Deliver Thing 7 to Person 10 in Instance 52, Zone 1
Talk to Person 8 in Instance 9, Zone 1

value.title: Relay Parts Courier
value.summary: Person 9 needs a replacement component brought over from Instance 9 without leaving their post at Instance 13.

steps.objective: Deliver Thing 2 to Person 9 at Instance 13.

value.name: The Copper Buoy
value.character: The Copper Buoy smells of stale stout, wet oilskins, and the brine-heavy fog leaking in from the dockside. A copper-plated mooring buoy hangs over the low timber counter, dented from decades of harbor drift and polished smooth near the tap pulls. In the corner of the taproom, an old monochrome CRT cabinet flickers with a low-volume game of Tetris, its rhythmic bleeps competing with the deep low-frequency drone vibrating up from the seabed telemetry arrays at low tide. Mechanics in grease-stained smocks and crane drivers from the basin huddle along the benches, keeping their voices low whenever red-coveralled Coreline technicians walk through the door.

people.name: Arthur Fletcher
people.personality: Nods curtly when you walk up, sliding a fresh coaster onto the timber counter before asking what you are drinking.
knowledge: Coreline survey divers drink bottled cider and always sit near the front door to watch who passes the street corner.
The cellar door latch sticks unless you pull up hard on the iron ring while turning the brass key.
Two drydock riggers owe twenty credits each on their slate since the crane pier lockdown started.

life.history: Born in Sound Point, he spent twenty years working harbor tugs until the offshore survey contracts replaced the local fleet. He bought The Copper Buoy with his redundancy payout and has kept its doors open through every dock strike and corporate buyout. When the scorched probe resurfaced three weeks ago, his taproom became neutral ground for nervous divers and desperate salvage hands.
life.interests: Tide charts, vintage brass bar fittings, and the high scores logged on the taproom arcade screen.
life.manner: Speaks in a dry, even gravel, wiping the counter methodically without breaking eye contact.
life.cares: Keeping the bar licensed, paying his distributor on time, and keeping his regulars from tearing each other apart.
life.avoids: Corporate litigation, inquiries about unrecorded cargo behind the cellar casks, and arguments between crane hands and divers.
life.reason: I am wiping down this counter and keeping the taps flowing so long as there are thirsty dock hands in town.
life.errand: I am walking to the supply shed to pick up a crate of dark ale and a fresh roll of till tape.

background.fact: Tends the bar at The Copper Buoy, drying glasses with a stained linen rag and keeping an eye on the door.
Used to run line-handling skiffs for the municipal pier before the telemetry firm bought out the lease and privatized the basin moorings.
Keeps the iron cellar key and back-room ledger locked under the counter to protect the basin salvage operators from corporate audits.
Took a hush-money advance from a Coreline liaison six months ago to ignore late-night canister drops in the taproom alley.

people.name: Thomas Grover
people.personality: Glances up sharply with narrowed eyes, gripping his glass until he confirms you are not carrying a corporate badge.
knowledge: The north shelf acoustic array is pulsing twice as fast since the probe surfaced three weeks ago.
The crane pier security guards change shifts every night at ten past nine, leaving the ladder unwatched for five minutes.
Coreline's salvage crew dropped an underwater torch near the slipway and never went back for it.

life.history: He grew up on the basin mudflats, apprenticing on the steam cranes before the survey boom brought automated winches. When Coreline Instruments locked down the main quay three weeks ago, his salvage crew was locked out without pay, leaving him with three months of overdue dock fees. Now he spends his afternoons watching the pier gate through the pub window, waiting for an opening.
life.interests: Heavy rigging cables, hydraulic winches, and the market price of scrap titanium.
life.manner: Speaks in short, blunt bursts, nervously rolling an iron bolt between his thick fingers.
life.cares: Getting the salvage pool back to work and recovering the telemetry core before the corporate dredgers scrape the seabed clean.
life.avoids: Red-coverall divers, Coreline legal notices, and talking about his mounting dock berth debt.
life.reason: I am waiting for the crane pier patrol to rotate so I can see if the water under the pilings has cleared.
life.errand: I am heading over to the machine shop to borrow a heavy cable cutter and a pair of dry gloves.

background.fact: Sits by the window with a half-empty glass of stout, watching the mist gather on the south conduit.
Works as a crane winch driver for the Basin Salvage Pool, currently laid off due to the dock lockdown.
Knows the exact submerged cable tangle under the old crane pier where the probe core got wedged during the storm.
Nearly drowned three years ago when an uncrewed survey tether snapped and dragged his launch into the breakwater.

people.name: Elena Faulkner
people.personality: Offers a polite, restrained nod, subtly angling her notebook away from view as you step close.
knowledge: The outdoor junction box on the south conduit sparks every time the onshore wind brings the salt spray in.
The optical core in the lost probe uses a dual-frequency laser ping that standard basin hydrophones cannot read.
The top score on the pub Tetris machine belongs to an offshore surveyor who disappeared last winter.

life.history: She moved to Sound Point four years ago on a Coreline technical contract, analyzing sub-sea acoustic data feeds. Over time she realized the deep telemetry arrays were picking up unexplained thermal anomalies along the trench shelf. When the scorched probe breached the surface, she refused to sign the company's non-disclosure annex and was quietly reassigned to graveyard desk shifts.
life.interests: Acoustic telemetry waveforms, fiber-optic cable splicing, and signal decoding algorithms.
life.manner: Quiet and precise, choosing her words carefully as if every sentence were being recorded by an auditor.
life.cares: Uncovering why the deep-trench probe returned six months early with scorched plating.
life.avoids: Direct questions about Coreline telemetry protocols, internal company audits, and company security officers.
life.reason: I am taking my break where the company microphones cannot pick up the hum of my diagnostic kit.
life.errand: I am going to check the signal amplifier on the roof mast to see if the shelf pings are drifting.

background.fact: Perches on a corner stool near the Tetris cabinet, nursing a cup of black tea with milk.
Employed as a night technician monitoring the deep-water telemetry buoys anchored across the shelf.
Wants to secure the encrypted pings from the scorched probe before Coreline wipes the server logs.
Her brother was a pilot on the uncrewed probe vessel that went missing six months before the casing resurfaced.

people.name: Marcus Young
people.personality: Steps aside swiftly with a guarded look, keeping his hands jammed deep into his heavy woolen coat pockets.
knowledge: A Coreline security skiff patrols the kelp beds every four hours between midnight and dawn.
The high tide mark under the old crane pier is choked with derelict steel mooring cables.
The back room of the bar is booked every Thursday night by the Basin Salvage Pool committee.

life.history: A lifelong coastal mariner who once ran cargo runs across the sound before corporate survey zones restricted open navigation. The sudden lockdown of the shoreline after the probe surfaced has choked off his livelihood, leaving him scrambling for freelance salvage work and scraps washed ashore along the bluffs.
life.interests: Coastal weather patterns, shallow draft skiff engines, and hidden coves along the north headland.
life.manner: Restless and gruff, constantly shifting his weight and glancing toward the street door.
life.cares: Keeping his skiff fueled and finding salable debris before the company cleanup crews comb the shoreline.
life.avoids: Harbor master inspections, patrol boats with searchlights, and paperwork from the marine registry.
life.reason: I am waiting for the fog to thicken enough so I can run my skiff out to the north reef without being spotted.
life.errand: I am walking down to the fuel jetty to see if the diesel barge has finished discharging its tanks.

background.fact: Paces between the bar and the entryway, checking the harbor fog through the frosted glass.
Operates an independent skiff hauling mail, light supplies, and salvage scrap along the rocky coast.
Found a buoyant titanium bracket from the exploded probe washed up on the gravel beach two miles north.
Lost his coastal pilot license two years ago after refusing to give right of way to a Coreline survey barge.

people.name: Clara Garrett
people.personality: Looks up from her map, giving you a measuring look before asking if you know anything about sub-sea hydraulics.
knowledge: The scorched probe plating was melted by intense heat that could not have come from electrical shorting.
The bar cellar contains three crates of discontinued deep-sea hydrophone parts from the old municipal yard.
The salvage pool mechanics meet at dawn near the slipway to swap tools before the security guards arrive.

life.history: She trained as an industrial shipwright before taking a job refitting uncrewed exploration probes for Coreline. She grew disillusioned when the firm began concealing structural failure reports on deep-trench equipment. When the scorched canister drifted into the basin, she threw her support behind the local salvage pool to expose the truth.
life.interests: High-temperature metallurgy, sub-sea pressure hulls, and precision gas cutting.
life.manner: Direct and practical, speaking with the steady confidence of an experienced metalworker.
life.cares: Proving that the probe's damage was caused by an external seabed event rather than mechanical failure.
life.avoids: Company tool requisitions, corporate security checkpoints, and inquiries regarding missing torch tanks.
life.reason: I am waiting for my shift partner to bring the torque specs for the probe's hatch assembly.
life.errand: I am heading to the ironmonger to pick up a box of carbide drill bits and high-pressure hose clamps.

background.fact: Leans against the timber pillar near the cellar door, studying a folded survey map.
Works as a mechanical welder repairing seabed probe chassis at the drydock basin.
Needs specialized ceramic cutting discs to breach the heat-tempered casing of a retrieved data canister.
Secretly fabricated the unauthorized dredging rig currently hidden beneath the basin salvage launch.

people.name: Nora Xavier
people.personality: Tenses slightly when you approach her booth, subtly setting her bottle down and keeping her shoulders square.
knowledge: Coreline's red-coverall dive teams are under strict orders not to discuss the probe's telemetry logs with locals.
The deep sonar hum increases in pitch right before the offshore testing buoys transmit their daily batch.
The bartender keeps a duplicate keycard to the company storage locker in a jar behind the cellar gin rack.

life.history: Recruited from an offshore commercial diving outfit, she spent three years running line tenders for deep telemetry platforms. She witnessed the scorched probe being hauled onto the barge three weeks ago and recognized that the telemetry core held vital data Coreline was desperate to suppress. Now she quietly feeds clues to local contacts while planning her exit.
life.interests: Sub-surface decompression tables, acoustic transponders, and maritime contract law.
life.manner: Speaks in hushed, guarded tones, frequently pausing to scan the room whenever the front door opens.
life.cares: Securing enough money to relocate out of Sound Point before Coreline discovers the leaked coordinates.
life.avoids: Company debriefings, internal security interrogators, and being seen talking to basin salvage mechanics.
life.reason: I am finishing my drink while waiting for the dockside surveillance drone to complete its scheduled sweep.
life.errand: I am walking to the coastal post box to mail a sealed dispatch to an independent maritime surveyor.

background.fact: Sits alone at a booth near the wall, methodically peeling the label off a cider bottle.
Works as an offshore dive tender for Coreline Operations, assisting trench retrieval teams.
Secretly copied the recovery coordinate overlay for the cable tangle under the old crane pier.
Is planning to resign from Coreline as soon as she sells her share of the salvage anomaly data.

people.name: Samuel Frost
people.personality: Smiles faintly without taking his eyes off the board, casually tossing another dart into the triple ring as you speak.
knowledge: The south gate padlock has a worn tumbler that can be jimmied with a flat screwdriver.
A courier from Coreline headquarters arrives on the morning train every Tuesday to collect raw telemetry disks.
The crane operator was arguing with the dive supervisor in the alley behind the pub yesterday evening.

life.history: A Sound Point native whose family worked the harbor docks for three generations. When the telemetry conglomerate took control of the municipal waterfront, he took a night watchman job to keep an eye on the drydocks. He uses his position to turn a blind eye when local salvage crews need to move equipment past the corporate perimeter.
life.interests: Lock mechanisms, dartboard games, and tracking the schedules of visiting corporate executive launches.
life.manner: Relaxed and worldly-wise, speaking with an easy drawl while retrieving his darts from the board.
life.cares: Protecting his childhood friends in the salvage pool from facing corporate prosecution.
life.avoids: Corporate incident reports, sobriety checks during night shifts, and daylight dock patrols.
life.reason: I am getting in a few rounds of darts before my ten-hour watch on the cold gatehouse post begins.
life.errand: I am walking over to the dock gatehouse to relieve the afternoon sentry and sign the gate manifest.

background.fact: Stands near the dartboard, tossing brass-tipped darts into the cork with methodical focus.
Works as a night watchman at the drydock gates, guarding the perimeter fence along the basin.
Allows basin salvage divers to slip through the side gate after hours in exchange for a cut of the scrap value.
Was formerly a sonar technician on the municipal survey vessel before Coreline dissolved the civic fleet.

people.name: Owen Yates
people.personality: Turns sharply with a firm grip on his work rag, evaluating you with a sharp, calculating stare.
knowledge: The physical telemetry core is still trapped in the old crane pier cable tangle six meters down.
The cellar beneath The Copper Buoy connects to an abandoned storm conduit leading straight to the basin shoreline.
Coreline's private security team is preparing to dredge the pier pilings within forty-eight hours.

life.history: He spent twenty-five years maintaining deep-water dredges and recovery rigs for the municipal port. When Coreline Instruments bought the harbor leases and privatized the basin, he organized the independent salvage mechanics into a collective. Now leading the race to salvage the scorched telemetry core, he operates out of the back room of The Copper Buoy to keep one step ahead of corporate injunctions.
life.interests: Underwater cutting torches, winch gear ratios, and deep-trench seafloor bathymetry.
life.manner: Authoritative and urgent, speaking with the gravelly determination of a veteran dock rigger.
life.cares: Recovering the scorched probe core before Coreline destroys the data and seizing the funds to save the basin docks.
life.avoids: Company security patrols, daylight waterfront walks, and anyone asking for his formal ID papers.
life.reason: I am waiting for my lead diver to report back on the cable tension under the old crane pier pilings.
life.errand: I am walking down to the shoreline culvert to inspect the low-tide clearance before tonight's salvage dive.

background.fact: Wipes grease from his hands with a kerosene rag while standing by the taproom cellar entrance.
Head maintenance rigger for the Basin Salvage Pool, coordinating underwater cable clearing under the piers.
Needs an encrypted telemetry decoder card brought to him to unlock the coordinates from the retrieved probe core.
Has an arrest warrant prepared against him by Coreline legal if he sets foot on the main quay pier.

things.name: Faded harbor oil painting
things.description: An oil painting in a salt-stained oak frame hanging behind the bar, depicting a three-masted schooner navigating the Sound Point reefs before the deep telemetry towers were installed.

things.name: Stained bar tab ledger
things.description: A thick, cloth-bound bar ledger with warped parchment pages, recording thirty years of dock worker bar tabs and uncollected debts from the municipal fleet.

things.name: Chipped heavy pint glass
things.description: A heavy, faceted pint glass chipped at the base, clouded from years of harsh salt-water washing and filled with dark ale.

things.name: Amber beach glass paperweight
things.description: A polished piece of raw amber washed up on the north breakers, mounted into a brass paperweight sitting beside the till.

things.name: Smudged brown paper envelope
things.description: A grease-smudged brown paper envelope tucked behind the till, containing handwritten shift rotations and patrol notes for the main quay gates.

things.name: Scuffed corporate telemetry keycard
things.description: A scuffed Coreline Instruments electronic keycard with a lanyard loop, bearing a faded security clearance stamp for the coastal telemetry junction boxes.

value.name: Crowell Freight
value.character: Crowell Freight smells of salt damp, machine grease, and old creosote planks. Stacks of palletized telemetry cable reels and heavy marine battery casings sit in rows under buzzing halogen strips, while a closed-circuit monitor flickers behind the guard desk watching the main rolling bay. Since the trench probe surfaced scorched off the breakers, the warehouse has been taking in nocturnal deliveries of locked aluminum transit trunks from the Basin Salvage Pool, kept strictly apart from the Coreline survey hardware tagged for the north shelf.

people.name: Derek Ellis
people.personality: Glances up from a flickering monitor with a squint, resting a calloused hand over his keys while sizing up whether you belong to Coreline or the salvage pool before speaking.
knowledge: The night door has been unlatched three times this week after the Coreline patrol vehicles finish their sweep of Conduit Street.
The camera pointed at the main floor has a bad ground wire that cuts the feed whenever the crane winch outside engages.
The heavy zinc trunks stacked in bay four aren't on the general freight manifest and came off a skiff without dock authority tags.
Acoustic telemetry buoys coming in from the north shelf have fresh burn marks along their seal gaskets.

life.history: Spent three decades working the winches on harbor salvage runs until a snapped hawser took his right knee out. When the survey boom started, Crowell took him on to watch the floor and manage the keys to the interior bays.
life.interests: Tide tables, winch gearing ratios, and the exact patrol schedule of the red-coverall Coreline security details.
life.manner: Speaks in a flat, gravelly drawl, keeping one hand resting on the heavy master key ring at his belt.
life.cares: Keeping the yard secure so his former tug crewmates in the Basin Salvage Pool don't get raided by Coreline security.
life.avoids: The exact serial numbers on the unmanifested zinc dive cases resting in bay four.
life.reason: I'm keeping watch over the freight bays and checking the camera log for anyone sniffing around the unmanifested crates.
life.errand: I'm carrying the night-gate key ring over to get a tooth filed down after it jammed in the foreman office padlock.

background.fact: Sits behind the battered desk with a ring of brass deadbolt keys hooked over his belt, watching the camera feed of the floor.
Worked thirty years as a winch engineer on the salvage tugs before a crushed knee put him on night watch at Crowell Freight.
Keeps the rear foreman's locker locked tight against Coreline auditors because it holds dredged recovery manifests belonging to his old tug crew.
Took five hundred notes from the Basin Salvage Pool to look away whenever unmanifested dive bags come through the side bay at low water.

things.name: stenciled freight crate
things.description: A reinforced marine plywood cargo crate banded with galvanized steel straps, stenciled with faded Coreline transit markings and soaked around the base from leaking bilge runoff.

value.name: 7 Cable Street
value.character: A damp, salt-scoured weatherboard house on the corner of Cable Street, officially listed for sale at 8223 credits while estate agents wait out the dock strikes. Inside, the floorboards vibrate faintly with the continuous hum of the north shelf sonar array, and salt mist creeps in through warped sash frames. While formally vacant, a handful of off-shift crane riggers and sub-sea survey hands from the Basin pool have quietly moved into the spare rooms to avoid company security dorms. An unconfigured display screen in the living room flickers with dead static, and the back bedroom remains padlocked where salvage recovery tools and dry acoustic telemetry loggers are stashed.

people.name: Arthur Latham
people.personality: Sits on a salt-bleached stool by the entrance hall radiator, turning a brass latch key over his knuckles while sizing up everyone who steps across the threshold.
knowledge: The estate agent only inspects the front porch on the second Tuesday of each month.
Coreline's private security van patrols Cable Street forty minutes after the evening tide turns.
The lock on the rear bedroom was replaced with a heavy brass deadbolt brought from the old boatyard.

life.history: Came to Sound Point from the river ports when Coreline expanded the acoustic monitoring shelf. After his winch accident at the crane pier, he moved into the vacant properties on Cable Street and now manages informal lodging for independent salvage hands.
life.interests: Tide tables, heavy wire splicing, and the sound of deep-water telemetry pings coming up through the floorboards.
life.manner: Speaks in a dry, measured rasp, pausing whenever a heavy lorry rumbles past down toward the slipway.
life.cares: Keeping the house unlocked for off-shift Basin divers who need a dry bed away from the quay guards.
life.avoids: Any talk about corporate indemnity forms or the company dispensary on Marek Lane.
life.reason: I keep the keys to this door and make sure nobody kicks the hallway wainscoting to splinters while the listing is open.
life.errand: Checking the conduit junction box down the lane before the salt mist shorts the streetlamps again.

background.fact: Carries the full ring of brass keys to the house and keeps a tally of everyone coming through the front door.
Worked six years as a crane tackle tender for Coreline until a snapped winch cable took his hearing in one ear.
Wants the Basin Salvage Pool to secure the sunken telemetry core so the local divers can pay off their drydock liens.
Brokered the quiet squatting arrangement with the estate agent's junior clerk in exchange for fresh seabed survey coordinates.

people.name: Ellen Upton
people.personality: Glances up sharply from her logbook, tracking your movement with a calm, analytical gaze before speaking.
knowledge: The living room monitor is wired into the municipal telemetry repeater, but it needs an active decryption key to show anything.
The neighbours two doors down argue every Thursday night over who left the outdoor conduit box unlatched.
Coreline divers in the red coveralls have been buying up spare oxygen scrubbers from independent chandlers.

life.history: Born and raised along the south reach of Sound Point. When the harbour authority folded into Coreline's operations, she refused a company badge and started logging offshore acoustic anomalies for the Basin Salvage Pool.
life.interests: Digital hydrophone schematics, coastal weather shifts, and optical data encoding.
life.manner: Quiet, watchful, and direct, keeping her eyes fixed on the door whenever voices raise in the corridor.
life.cares: Preserving independent acoustic access to the shelf so local skiffs can navigate without corporate permits.
life.avoids: Signing survey manifests or mentioning her family's dock debts to strangers.
life.reason: I am waiting for the telemetry feed to clear up on this monitor so we can see where the surge carried the canister.
life.errand: Fetching a fresh set of dry batteries for the telemetry receiver before nightfall.

background.fact: Spends her afternoons sitting by the cold living room fireplace checking handwritten cable logs against the inactive wall screen.
Operated shallow survey drones for the municipal harbour authority before Coreline bought out the boatyard lease.
Fears that corporate auditors will seize her father's old salvage skiff if the lost data canisters are tied to her family.
Maintains a hidden copy of the living room screen's diagnostic firmware hidden inside an old oilcloth binder.

people.name: Martin Walsh
people.personality: Wipes flour and grease from his apron with a broad grin, immediately offering a warm mug of chicory brew before you can ask your question.
knowledge: The tap water in the kitchen runs brackish whenever the deep pumps on the pier run at full pressure.
The crane crews on the pier will trade fresh cod for strong coffee and dry work gloves.
Coreline's shore patrol never checks the kitchen delivery door behind the coal bunker.

life.history: Worked galleys along the coast until the sub-sea survey boom brought industrial barges into Sound Point. He took up the kitchen at 7 Cable Street to cook communal meals for the displaced salvage crews.
life.interests: Cast-iron cookware, preserving fish in sea salt, and old shanties from the coal-haul days.
life.manner: Cheery and gruff, talking with his hands while wiping down grease off a tin mug with a checkered tea towel.
life.cares: Making sure every diver and mechanic coming off the cold night water gets a hot meal and dry wool.
life.avoids: Corporate salvage politics, company inspectors, and arguments over dock boundary lines.
life.reason: Somebody has to keep the stove lit and feed the divers coming off the low tide before they freeze to the bone.
life.errand: Carrying a thermos of broth and fresh bread down toward the breakwater workers.

background.fact: Stands over the iron range in the kitchen, boiling salt beef and chicory coffee for the house occupants.
Ran the galley on an offshore acoustic cable-laying barge for eleven years before dock work slowed down.
Is hoarding tins of dry rations in the pantry to support the salvage crews if the quay is fully sealed off.
Owes forty credits to the fishmonger for a crate of smoked mackerel he gave to the crane riggers on credit.

people.name: Sarah Abbott
people.personality: Stands stiffly beside her workbench, holding a wire brush mid-stroke while listening closely to your footsteps on the floorboards.
knowledge: The scorched probe suffered an external thermal surge at four thousand metres, not an internal battery blowout.
Two data canisters broke loose along the shallow kelp line near the old crane pier.
The locked back bedroom holds three acoustic locators salvaged from the breaker line.

life.history: Recruited straight out of technical school to maintain uncrewed seabed probes for Coreline. After inspecting the melted telemetry core from the trench probe, she realized the company planned to falsify the report and walked off the job.
life.interests: Pressure seals, optical cabling, and thermal imaging of sub-sea trenches.
life.manner: Tense, rapid-fire, and precise, frequently looking over her shoulder toward the window facing the quay.
life.cares: Proving that the scorched seabed probe encountered an unmapped underwater power surge.
life.avoids: Discussing company non-disclosure contracts or meeting anyone carrying a corporate security badge.
life.reason: I am checking these optical couplers before the evening salvage skiff heads out under the crane pier.
life.errand: Picking up a replacement optical lens gasket from the drydock workshop.

background.fact: Occupies the small upstairs bedroom, constantly cleaning salt grime off sub-sea camera housings.
Worked as a seabed probe mechanic for Coreline until the scorched probe resurfaced off the breakers three weeks ago.
Wants to expose Coreline's unlawful deep-trench dredging before corporate auditors cover up the seabed anomaly.
Left her company locker key with the mechanic on Marlin Lane when she slipped away from the quay.

things.name: Rigging canvas bag
things.description: A waxed canvas duffel bag stained with motor grease and sea salt, packed with dry wool socks and brass winch pins.

things.name: Sealed telemetry briefcase
things.description: A battered aluminium briefcase with scratched corner brackets, sealed with a strip of waterproof electrical tape across the latch.

things.name: Potted sea aster
things.description: A hardy sea aster in a chipped ceramic pot on the kitchen windowsill, coated in a fine layer of coastal salt dust.

things.name: Tide and cable logbook
things.description: A water-swollen clothbound ledger filled with handwritten tidal depths, cable coordinates, and sonar frequencies.
